# Liquid Crystal Display Device with Touch Detection Functionality

## Overview

The present invention aims to provide a liquid crystal display device with touch detection functionality that is capable of accommodating any drive method. By offering flexibility in the manner in which the device is driven, the invention addresses the need for a versatile display solution that can be adapted to various operational requirements and configurations.

## Display Element and Scanning Line Configuration

The device includes a plurality of liquid crystal display elements arranged in a matrix formation. Each of these display elements is paired with corresponding scanning lines, which are configured to supply scanning signals to each respective row of the matrix. Through this arrangement, the scanning signals are systematically delivered to the display elements on a row-by-row basis, thereby enabling controlled activation of the display.

## Signal Line Arrangement

In addition to the scanning lines, signal lines are arranged in each column of the matrix. These signal lines are responsible for supplying image signals to the liquid crystal display elements located within the corresponding column. As a result, the combination of scanning lines and signal lines allows for precise control over each individual display element, ensuring accurate image reproduction across the entire display area.

## Touch Detection Drive Electrodes

The device further incorporates multiple touch detection drive electrodes, which are arranged in a column. These electrodes are configured to receive a drive signal that is used for the purpose of detecting touch input. By integrating these drive electrodes into the structure of the display, the device is able to perform touch detection in conjunction with its display functions.

## Touch Control Operation

A touch control part is provided to manage the touch detection process. Specifically, the touch control part specifies a particular touch detection drive electrode from among the multiple electrodes. Once the electrode has been specified, the drive signal is supplied to that designated electrode. This selective supply of the drive signal enables efficient and targeted touch detection, contributing to the overall adaptability of the device with respect to different drive methods.

# Liquid Crystal Display Device with Integrated Touch Detection Functionality

## Overview

A liquid crystal display device incorporating touch detection functionality has been developed to combine visual display capabilities with responsive touch-sensing technology in a single integrated unit. This device represents an advancement in display technology by embedding touch detection components directly within the liquid crystal display structure, eliminating the need for separate touch panel layers and improving overall device efficiency.

## Device Configuration

The core of this device consists of liquid crystal display elements arranged in a matrix formation. This matrix architecture is supported by several key structural components working in coordination:

- **Scanning Lines:** These lines run across the display to sequentially activate rows of pixels, controlling when each row is addressed during the display operation.

- **Signal Lines:** Positioned to intersect with the scanning lines, these carry the image data signals that determine the visual output of individual pixels within the matrix.

- **Touch Detection Drive Electrodes:** These specialized electrodes are integrated into the display structure to enable touch-sensing capabilities. They serve a dual purpose, participating in both the display function and the touch detection process.

- **Touch Control Part:** This is the intelligent management component of the system, responsible for specifying which particular electrode is designated to receive the drive signal at any given moment.

## Operational Principle

The distinctive feature of this design lies in its selective signal distribution mechanism. Rather than applying drive signals uniformly, the touch control part precisely specifies which touch detection drive electrode should receive the drive signal. This targeted approach ensures that the drive signal is selectively supplied only to the designated electrode.

## Advantages and Flexibility

The primary benefit of this configuration is the flexibility it provides in touch detection methodology. Because the drive signal can be directed to any specified touch detection drive electrode as determined by the touch control part, the system is not limited to a single predetermined driving scheme. Instead, virtually any drive method can be adopted for the touch detection function.

This adaptability allows the device to accommodate various operational requirements, optimize performance under different conditions, and support diverse touch detection strategies, making the display device versatile and suitable for a wide range of applications.

# The Power of "The" and "Here"

Some of the smallest words in the English language carry the greatest weight. Two perfect examples are "the" and "here"—words we use countless times each day, often without a second thought, yet which shape the very way we communicate and understand the world around us.

## The Definite Article

"The" is one of the most frequently used words in the English language. As the only definite article, it does something remarkable: it points to something specific and known. When we say "the book," we aren't talking about just any book—we're referring to *the* particular one that both speaker and listener recognize. This tiny word transforms vague ideas into concrete references, guiding our attention to exactly what matters.

Without "the," language would feel unanchored. It gives our sentences precision, allowing us to distinguish between the general and the particular, the abstract and the real.

## Here and Now

"Here" grounds us in place and presence. It marks the spot where we stand, both physically and metaphorically. When someone says "come here," they invite you into their space. When we say "here we are," we acknowledge a moment fully arrived.

"Here" is intimately tied to the present—to being aware, engaged, and alive in this exact location and time. It reminds us that experience always happens *somewhere*, and that somewhere is usually right where we are.

## Small Words, Big Meaning

Together, "the" and "here" demonstrate that significance isn't measured by length. These humble words do the quiet, essential work of anchoring our thoughts, directing our focus, and connecting us to the specific realities of the present moment.

The next time you use them, consider the invisible power they hold—right here, in the very words you speak.

# Patent Abstract

## Liquid Crystal Display Device with Touch Detection Functionality Supporting Flexible Drive Methods

**Abstract**

A liquid crystal display device with integrated touch detection functionality is disclosed, comprising a display panel having a plurality of pixel electrodes arranged in a matrix, a common electrode configured to operate selectively as a display drive electrode and a touch detection drive electrode, and a plurality of touch detection electrodes arranged to face the common electrode. A control circuit is configured to selectively execute a plurality of drive methods including a first drive mode in which display operations and touch detection operations are performed in a time-divisional manner within a single display frame period, and a second drive mode in which display operations and touch detection operations are performed simultaneously. The device further includes a drive selection unit that dynamically switches between the drive methods based on operational parameters such as display content, power consumption requirements, refresh rate, and touch sensitivity demands. The common electrode is divided into a plurality of segments that can be independently addressed, enabling flexible allocation of drive signals for concurrent display refresh and capacitance-based touch sensing across selectable regions of the panel. This configuration reduces electrical interference between display and touch functions, improves signal-to-noise ratio in touch detection, and optimizes power efficiency while maintaining high display quality. The flexible drive architecture allows the device to adapt to varying application requirements without hardware modification, thereby providing enhanced versatility for use in mobile devices, tablets, and other interactive display applications.

---

counterfactuals.output:
# LCD Device with Integrated Touch Sensor: Technical Solution Summary

## Overview
This invention relates to a liquid crystal display (LCD) device that incorporates touch-sensing functionality directly within the display structure, eliminating the need for a separate external touch panel layer.

## Main Components

### 1. Display Panel Structure
- **Upper substrate** (color filter substrate)
- **Lower substrate** (TFT array substrate)
- **Liquid crystal layer** sandwiched between the two substrates
- **Polarizers** on outer surfaces to control light transmission

### 2. Touch-Sensing Elements
- **Sensing electrodes** integrated into the panel, often sharing or reusing existing display electrodes (such as common electrodes)
- **Drive electrodes** that work with sensing electrodes to detect capacitance changes
- **Touch controller/driver IC** to process signals from the sensing array

### 3. Integration Approach
The touch sensor is embedded using one of these architectures:
- **In-cell**: Touch sensors placed *inside* the LCD cell (within the liquid crystal layer region)
- **On-cell**: Touch sensors placed *on* the outer surface of the color filter substrate

## Technical Solution

### Time-Division / Multiplexing
The device typically operates in **time-shared periods**:
- **Display period**: Electrodes function to drive the liquid crystal for image display
- **Touch-sensing period**: The same electrodes are switched to detect touch inputs

### Capacitive Sensing
Touch detection relies on **capacitance variation**—when a finger approaches, it changes the capacitance between electrodes, which is measured to determine touch coordinates.

## Key Advantages
- **Reduced thickness** and lighter weight
- **Improved optical clarity** (fewer layers)
- **Lower manufacturing cost** through component sharing
- **Simplified assembly** process

---

# Abstract

A touch-enabled liquid crystal display device is disclosed, comprising a display panel that integrates image display and touch detection functionality. The device includes a plurality of scanning lines extending in a first direction and a plurality of signal lines extending in a second direction intersecting the scanning lines, the scanning lines and signal lines cooperating to define a matrix of pixel regions for image display. A plurality of pixel electrodes and switching elements, such as thin-film transistors, are disposed at intersections of the scanning lines and signal lines to control display operations.

The display device further comprises a plurality of touch detection drive electrodes arranged within the display panel, wherein the touch detection drive electrodes are configured to selectively serve a dual function by operating as common electrodes for image display during a display period and as drive electrodes for touch sensing during a touch detection period. The touch detection drive electrodes are supplied with drive signals in a time-division manner relative to the display drive operations, thereby enabling both display and touch functions without requiring a separate touch panel layer.

A touch control part is provided in electrical communication with the touch detection drive electrodes and associated detection electrodes. The touch control part supplies touch drive signals to the touch detection drive electrodes and receives detection signals indicative of capacitance variations arising from a proximity or contact of an external object, such as a finger or stylus. Based on the received detection signals, the touch control part determines the presence and coordinate position of a touch input on the display surface.

By integrating the scanning lines, signal lines, touch detection drive electrodes, and touch control part within a unified panel structure, the disclosed device achieves reduced thickness, simplified manufacturing, and improved display quality while providing accurate and responsive touch detection.

# Patent Abstract

## In-Cell Touch LCD Panel with Selective Drive Signal Supply to Touch Detection Electrodes

### Problem

Conventional in-cell touch liquid crystal display (LCD) panels integrate touch sensing electrodes within the display cell structure, wherein common electrodes are typically time-shared between display driving operations and touch detection operations. However, such configurations suffer from several drawbacks: (1) supplying drive signals simultaneously to all touch detection electrodes across the entire panel consumes excessive power and generates substantial electromagnetic interference that degrades touch detection accuracy; (2) display noise coupled into the touch electrodes reduces the signal-to-noise ratio, particularly in larger panels; and (3) the increased loading from driving numerous electrodes concurrently limits the achievable touch scanning speed and responsiveness. These limitations compromise touch sensitivity, increase power consumption, and constrain overall device performance.

### Solution

The present invention provides an in-cell touch LCD panel comprising a plurality of touch detection electrodes arranged within the display cell and a drive circuit configured to selectively supply drive signals to **specified touch detection electrodes** rather than to all electrodes uniformly. The drive circuit identifies a target subset of touch detection electrodes—for example, those corresponding to a region of anticipated or detected user contact—and applies drive signals exclusively to the specified electrodes during a touch detection period. Non-specified electrodes may be held at a reference potential or supplied with a shielding signal to suppress noise coupling.

By restricting drive signal supply to specified touch detection electrodes, the invention reduces power consumption, minimizes electromagnetic interference, improves the signal-to-noise ratio of touch detection, and enables faster and more accurate touch sensing. This selective driving scheme thereby enhances the overall performance and efficiency of the in-cell touch LCD panel while maintaining a thin, integrated device structure.
